_comment: Example only. The real file lives at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/llms/settings.json
and is never committed: it is host state (binary paths, device pins, VRAM budget).
Create it with `llms init --server <llama-server>`, then add engines as below.
Every key is optional except the ones llms init writes. LLMS_* environment
variables override these; LLMS_ENGINES takes a JSON object.
An engine names a local server process. Registry entries refer to one by
logical name, so the same registry works on this host and on a CUDA box:
only this file changes.
Engine keys:
server          required; absolute path, or relative to cwd, or a name on PATH
kind            'llama.cpp' (default) composes -m/-c/-np/--kv-unified and
${common} from the registry entry; 'custom' passes only the
engine args plus the entry's extra_args, for servers that are
not llama.cpp and take none of those flags
args            fixed arguments always passed to this engine
env             injected into the process; llama-swap requires UPPER_CASE names.
This is where device pins belong: MESA_VK_DEVICE_SELECT only
affects Vulkan, HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES only affects HIP, and
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES only affects CUDA. A pin set on the systemd
unit applies to every backend indiscriminately, which is wrong.
cwd             absolute; rendered with env --chdir so no shell is involved and
signals still reach the server process directly
check_endpoint  health path, or 'none' to skip
use_model_name  model id to send upstream when it differs from the registry id
unload_timeout  graceful seconds before force-kill
--host/--port ${PORT} are appended automatically for every engine.
